newsitem.title: USA: US debt futures end higher after dramatic reversal.
newsitem.headline: US debt futures end higher after dramatic reversal.

text.p: U.S. debt futures closed higher after dramatically reversing the day's losses which were set in a knee-jerk reaction to the rise in U.S. February nonfarm payrolls, traders and analysts said.
June T-bonds extended their downtrend to 108-23/32, below the five-month low of 108-23/32, after the 339,000-increase in February payrolls initially sparked inflationay concerns.
However, the rest of the data did not point to an increase in price pressures, and gave shorts a reason to cover.
"It was a reversal day," Gerry Hildebrandt, senior vice president of ING, said. "We made a new low and then rallied."
June T-bonds set an outside range day in which a widely swinging market results in a price range where the high is higher and the low is lower than the previous day's activity.

Hildebrandt said shorts accumulated positions at the opening, which forced an even greater amount of the positions to be covered later in the day. Short-term conditions in both T-bonds and Eurodollars have been extremely oversold all week.
"This is merely a function of technical short-covering," another trader said. "It's definitely a contrarian bounce."
He and other market sources said the market was still bracing for a rate tightening by the U.S. Federal Reserve.
"The data this morning gave us no reason to change the fundamental outlook," one T-bond futures floor source said.
The lower-than-expected rise in average hourly earnings, and the downwardly revised gain in December payrolls contributed to the positive technical factors.

"We bounced off seven percent (on long bond yield), which must have represented good value to some," Hildebrandt said. The seven percent yield level is roughly equivalent to the June bond session low of 108-23/32, he said.
Many traders and analysts said a bounce from a test of the seven percent level was widely anticipated.
Floor traders said shorts were forced to cover positions again when June T-bonds blew through the 109-29/32 level.
"There were quite a few distressed shorts who had to cover when we rose through 109-29/32," one floor broker said.

September Eurodollars rose through the 200-day moving average of 93.85, while the June to June calendar spread narrowed slightly to 61 basis points after trading at nearly 64 basis points this morning.

September fell through the lower weekly Bollinger band at 93.89, but bounced above that level so quickly that some technicians discounted the bearish implications of the move. Eurodollar trader said. "After Greenspan's testimony -- it was like he was warning everybody."
June T-bonds backed down to 110-01/32 on light activity late in the day. Except near the close, trade was heavy and active all day.

At the end of pit trade, June T-bonds were up 18/32 at 110-03/32, 10-year notes were up 12/32 at 107-19/32, June T-bills were up 0.02 at 94.75, June Eurodollars were up 0.04 at 94.20 and September Eurodollars rose 0.055 at 94.00. ((Derivatives desk 312-408-8750;E-mail derivatives@reuters.com))
